description: KEY cortex commands are attributed to the authenticated member (R0-09-ID-HARDEN review R09-ST-4 and CR-3; R0-34b review ST-3). Every KeyCortexController handler that hands a user to a service takes it from @CurrentUser() (the principal AuthGuard admitted) through requestActorId; a body or query userId naming someone else is IGNORED (pinned: not refused; the DTOs keep it as an optional string), and with no authenticated user the handler answers 401 instead of running as 'system', 'key_user' or nobody. The KEY settings adapter applies IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner (owner ruling D-11) on the command's actor with its User role before settings.update_business_profile and settings.update_branding: a STAFF or ADMIN (settings:write) command answers 200 with the connector failure shape (result.success false, 'Only the business owner can edit the business profile') and leaves the Business row byte-identical; the OWNER membership, the Business.ownerId owner and SUPER_ADMIN succeed. Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/key-cortex-actor-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/key-cortex/adapters/settings-adapter.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex.controller.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-09c-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/key-cortex-actor-binding.json --report .proof/r0-09c-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE (claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at a230d7fc, tests-first commit 3a6b4076): the real-database suite failed 15 of 22 (execute with body userId=OWNER ran the command as the OWNER; execute with no userId ran as 'system'; the natural-language path parsed and built for the body user; POST query routed its command with userId undefined; rollback named 'system'; batch named the body user for every command; STAFF and ADMIN settings.update_business_profile / update_branding succeeded and changed the row; conscious/stream, conscious/chat and POST sessions wrote CortexSession rows for the outsider named in the request; chat, chat/stream and stream handed the reasoning engine the request user, stream 'key_user' when none; GET sessions?userId=OWNER listed the OWNER's session to a STAFF member; feedback recorded the outsider). The settings-adapter spec failed 9 of 21 and the controller spec 9 of 19. Cases without RED-BEFORE passed before the fix and are controls (AuthGuard 401, BusinessGuard 403 for a member of another business, OWNER and SUPER_ADMIN writes, delegation of the other settings actions). After the red run, three execute cases were changed from an exact list of routed commands to the command plus at most its compensating revert_<action> (the executor's rollbackOnFailure attempt, which runs only once the adapter refuses), every one still for the STAFF member.
notes: Out of scope, left to V1-03-KEY-CORTEX-PRINCIPAL (blocked on D-17): autonomy-profile write authority (who may change tiers and the kill switch: PATCH autonomy-profile is still membership-only) and the autonomy orchestrator's use of proposedBy beyond receiving the authenticated id (the suite's orchestrator is a recording stand-in).

GET sessions now lists the authenticated user's own sessions (it listed every session of the business when no ?userId was sent, or the named user's). GET messages with no sessionId still falls back to the business's most recent session, whoever owns it, and GET/PATCH/DELETE sessions/:id check no session owner: within-tenant session privacy, recorded for a follow-up, not changed here.

Discovered, outside this write set: KeyCortexGoalsController createPlanFromGoal and createPlanFromCommand still hand the planner dto.userId (key-cortex-goals.controller.ts), and the planner executes commands through KeyCortexExecutorService with it, so a spoofed actor can still reach the settings adapter that way; KeyCortexExecutorService.logExecution writes fields AiExecutionLog does not have (traceId, parameters, commandJson, ...), so every execute logs 'Failed to persist audit log' and no ai_execution_logs row is written (observed in this suite).

POST query routes its 'query' name to the module adapter as a command like any other (settings.update_business_profile included); it now names the authenticated actor, so the owner rule applies there too.
